sections.h2: What are my choices for a fast sale in North Miami?
sections.html:
Three routes exist: a cash buyer, an agent listing, or a sale you run yourself. Which fits depends on your deadline and on how much work the house needs. The deed, the title search and Miami-Dade recording work the same way on each path. What differs is who pays for repairs, how long you wait and what you keep.

  • Cash buyer: fewer contingencies, a negotiable closing date, house taken as is.
  • Agent listing: a larger pool of buyers, with showings, an inspection period and a lender's schedule.
  • Owner sale: no listing fee, but the contract and screening are yours.

Collect at least two written numbers and compare the net you would keep.

North Miami is a suburban city in northeast Miami-Dade County, about ten miles north of downtown Miami, and its own communications describe it as the sixth largest city in the county with more than 64,000 residents. The city dates its incorporation to February 5, 1926, and it marked its centennial in 2026 with a year of events centered on downtown around NE 125th Street.

Biscayne Bay lies along its eastern side, and the Biscayne Bay Campus of Florida International University is nearby. The city also lists the Oleta River State Park, the largest urban park in the Florida State Park System, and the Museum of Contemporary Art at MOCA Plaza among its landmarks. Homes near the water and near the university draw different buyers than homes inland, and renters and investors are a steady part of the market.

sections.h2: What local rules should I check before I sell in North Miami?
sections.html:
Start with the code compliance office, because its published answers cover parking, right-of-way upkeep and rentals. Its FAQ says violation notices go to the property owner, not the tenant, so an open violation on your address is your problem to clear before closing.

Rentals are tightly limited. The city's FAQ states that advertising a rental for less than three months is prohibited, and that renting for three months or less, or renting more than four times in a twelve month period, is prohibited. If your house has been used for short stays, a buyer will ask about it, and you should stop before listing.

  • Ask code compliance whether the address has open violations or an unfinished inspection.
  • Keep the right-of-way in front of the lot maintained, since owners are responsible for it.
  • Do not divide a single-family home into units without permits from the city's Building Department.
  • Ask whether a certificate of use or business tax receipt is attached to the property.

The city's code compliance phone line is listed on its site, and calling it before you list is cheaper than learning about a problem from the buyer's title company.

sections.h2: How much does a North Miami closing cost in taxes and fees?
sections.html:
Deed stamp tax is the largest state item, and Miami-Dade sets its own schedule. The state's revenue department prints 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax, with the surtax left off a document that conveys only a single-family dwelling. Elsewhere in Florida the rate is 70 cents.

Closing items on a North Miami deed, from official Florida pages
ItemWhat the official page says
Deed stamp tax, Miami-Dade60 cents per $100, plus 45 cents per $100 surtax (not due on a single-family dwelling only)
Liability for the taxAll parties to the document are liable
Clerk recording, first page$5.00
Clerk recording, each added page$4.00
Collected byThe county clerk when the deed is recorded

The statute also lists small extra charges per page, so the title company's settlement statement is the place to see the final recording total. Mortgage payoffs, association fees and prorated property tax come out of your proceeds at closing.

sections.h2: How does the county tax bill figure into my sale?
sections.html:
Each January 1 fixes the assessed value, and the tax collector sends bills in November. The state calendar has the proposed tax notice going out in August, and the Miami-Dade appraiser's homestead page says exemption applications are due March 1 and late ones are accepted until the deadline printed on the proposed notice, usually 25 days after it is mailed.

The homestead exemption belongs to you, not the house. When you sell, the buyer files a new application, and a sale resets the assessed value to market level the following January 1. The appraiser's page also warns that renewal receipts are not sent to properties with a change of ownership, including by warranty or quitclaim deed.

The same page describes Amendment 3, approved by Florida voters on November 3, 2026, which raises the non-school homestead exemption to $150,000 for tax year 2027 and $250,000 for 2028 for owners who established residency by December 31, 2026. A buyer's future bill may look quite different from yours, so ask a title or tax professional before you make claims about it in a listing.

sections.h2: What about an inherited or tenant occupied house?
sections.html:
Yes to both, with conditions. An inherited house needs someone with authority to sign, so the title company will ask for probate letters or proof the property passed outside probate. The state's list shows a personal representative's deed under a probated will as one that owes no stamp tax.

With a tenant, hand the buyer the lease and deposit details. Some cash buyers accept the tenant and others want the unit empty at closing. North Miami limits short rentals, so confirm any short-stay use was lawful before you describe it.

Moving the house to a relative first can add cost, since quitclaim deeds are on the taxable list and may change how the county treats ownership.

sections.h2: What is a sensible timeline for a sale?
sections.html:
With clean title a cash sale can wrap up in a couple of weeks. A financed sale runs longer because of the appraisal and loan approval. Allow time for payoff letters, an association estoppel and clearing any permit or violation.

  • First week: gather the deed, tax bill, payoff and association papers.
  • Next: pick an offer and a closing date.
  • Then: title search, lien and violation clearing, signing appointment.
  • Closing: signing before witnesses or a notary, then recording.

A contract with a firm date and a plain list of seller repairs prevents the most common slips.

faqs.q: What is the stamp tax rate on a deed in North Miami?
faqs.a: Miami-Dade charges 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax, per the state revenue department, and the surtax is not due when only a single-family dwelling is transferred. Your title company can give the figure for your deed.

faqs.q: Can I rent the house short term while it is listed?
faqs.a: The city's published answer says rentals of three months or less are prohibited, as is renting more than four times in twelve months. Check with code compliance before any short stay.

faqs.q: Does the buyer inherit my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. The buyer applies to the Miami-Dade Property Appraiser by March 1, and the sale resets assessed value to market level the next January 1.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for a code violation notice at my address?
faqs.a: The city addresses the notice to the owner. A tenant should speak with the landlord, but plan to clear the violation before closing.

faqs.q: What is Amendment 3 and when does it start?
faqs.a: The county appraiser reports that voters approved it on November 3, 2026. It takes effect January 1, 2027 and first applies to the 2027 tax year, raising the non-school homestead exemption for eligible owners.
